about: Ember's problem library. "problems" are stated in her typed language: each task is a problem she can run with autonomous_research, and the query open_problems lets her choose one herself. Open and closed problems state a question itself; a window (status "window") states a finite exact view of a catalog problem, computed or verified by one of her window tools, and settles nothing about it. "catalog" lists open problems she cannot state yet; each names what her language lacks, described under "needs", and points to its window when it has one. "tools" lists the window tools and the needs each looks into; "resolved" lists problems that left the catalog when the literature settled them. Her choice reads only the id, status and task of a stated problem. Everything else is for people: it was written from secondary knowledge, statuses were checked by web search where "checked" says so, and none of it is evidence she uses.

problems.title: Erdős–Straus conjecture
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: Her theorems prove the statement for every n from the least n outside the residue classes her covers leave open, and her range checks every n below 100,000. Her own checked lemma shows that no classical fixed-parameter family reaches a coprime square class, so for 4/n covers of this kind cannot settle it.
problems.known: Open. Mordell showed it for every n outside six residue classes mod 840 (the squares 1, 121, 169, 289, 361, 529). Verified for every n <= 10^18 (Mihnea and Dumitru, arXiv 2025, a preprint, extending Salez, arXiv 2014, n <= 10^17). Her Campaign 1 reduced it to 26,262 classes mod 36,756,720 (CAMPAIGNS.md).
problems.source: Erdős and Straus (1948); Mordell, Diophantine Equations (1969).

problems.known: Open for a = 6 as for every a >= 4. For even n = 2m, 6/n = 3/m, which is always a sum of three unit fractions.

problems.title: Collatz conjecture
problems.statement: Every orbit of T(n) = n/2 (n even), (3n + 1)/2 (n odd) from a positive integer reaches 1.
problems.scope: Her descent covers prove that every n in a covered class modulo 2^20 falls below itself, and her range checks every n below 10^6. The class of 2^k - 1 modulo 2^k never descends within k steps, so no finite depth settles the conjecture in this language.
problems.known: Open. Verified by computer far beyond her range (Barina, 2025); Tao (2019) proved that almost all orbits attain almost bounded values.
problems.source: Collatz (1937); Lagarias, The 3x + 1 Problem and Its Generalizations (1985).

problems.title: The Collatz stopping-time sieve to 2^18
problems.statement: Count the residue classes modulo 2^k, for k = 1 to 18, on which T^j(n) < n is not certified within k steps.
problems.scope: A closed count: her open classes at each level can be compared with an independent parity simulation.
problems.known: Closed. 7,495 classes mod 2^18 stay open; her Campaign 3 matched all 18 levels against an independent count.
problems.source: The stopping-time sieve is classical (Terras 1976; Everett 1977).

problems.title: Three unit fractions for 3/n
problems.statement: For every integer n >= 2, 3/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
problems.scope: A theorem with no open residue proves the statement for every n >= 2.
problems.known: True: 3/n = 1/n + 1/n + 1/n. A calibration of the settled path for covers.

problems.title: Descent of the halving map
problems.statement: Under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (n + 1)/2 (n odd), every n >= 2 has some j >= 1 with T^j(n) < n.
problems.scope: A descent cover reaching every class of its modulus, with a range from 2 to its bound, proves the statement.
problems.known: True in one step. A calibration of the settled path for descent.

problems.title: Descent of the 3n - 1 map
problems.statement: Under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (3n - 1)/2 (n odd), every n >= 2 has some j >= 1 with T^j(n) < n.
problems.scope: A checked cycle avoiding 1 refutes the statement: its least member never falls below itself.
problems.known: False: 5 -> 7 -> 10 -> 5 is a cycle. Refutation practice.

problems.title: Descent of the 5n + 1 map
problems.statement: Under T(n) = n/2 (n even), (5n + 1)/2 (n odd), every n >= 2 has some j >= 1 with T^j(n) < n.
problems.scope: A checked cycle avoiding 1 refutes the statement: its least member never falls below itself.
problems.known: False: 13 -> 33 -> 83 -> 208 -> 104 -> 52 -> 26 -> 13 is a cycle. Refutation practice. Whether the orbit of 7 is unbounded is open and listed in the catalog.

problems.title: Window: Riemann hypothesis
problems.statement: The sign of Hardy's Z(t) at t = 10, 10.2, ..., 49.8, each change of sign being a zero of zeta on the critical line, and a certified upper bound on the number of zeros with 0 < Im s < 50.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The zeros below height 50 have imaginary parts about 14.13, 21.02, 25.01, 30.42, 32.94, 37.59, 40.92, 43.33, 48.01 and 49.77 (Odlyzko's tables); every zero up to height 3·10^12 lies on the line (Platt and Trudgian, 2021).
problems.source: Riemann (1859); a Clay Millennium Prize Problem (2000).

problems.title: Window: Generalized Riemann hypothesis
problems.statement: The sign of the real form of L(1/2 + it, chi_4), chi_4 the nontrivial character mod 4, at t = 1, 1.2, ..., 30.8; each change of sign is a zero of L(s, chi_4) on the critical line.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The lowest zero of L(s, chi_4) on the critical line lies near height 6.0209 (LMFDB).

problems.title: Window: Lindelöf hypothesis
problems.statement: Over t = 100, 100.25, ..., 149.75: the point where the certified lower bound on |zeta(1/2 + it)| is largest, with that bound: a certified lower bound on how large zeta gets on this stretch of the critical line.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Lindelöf predicts |zeta(1/2 + it)| = O(t^eps) for every eps > 0; the best proved exponent is 13/84 (Bourgain, 2017).
problems.source: Lindelöf (1908); implied by the Riemann hypothesis.

problems.title: Window: Gauss circle problem
problems.statement: For every integer radius r <= 2000: the exact number of lattice points in the disc of radius r, and a certified upper bound on the largest |N(r) - pi r^2| / r^(1/2).
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The conjecture is |N(r) - pi r^2| = O(r^(1/2 + eps)); the best proved exponent is 131/208 (Huxley, 2003).
problems.source: Gauss; Hardy (1915) showed that 1/2 cannot be lowered.

problems.known: The conjectured error exponent is 1/4 + eps; the best proved exponent is 131/416 (Huxley, 2003).

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.source: Mersenne (1644); the question of infinitude is folklore.

problems.title: Window: Fermat primes beyond 65537
problems.statement: Every n <= 13 with 2^(2^n) + 1 prime, by Pepin's test.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: F_0 to F_4 are prime; F_5 to F_32 are known composite.
problems.source: Fermat (1640) conjectured all are prime; Euler (1732) factored the case n = 5.

problems.title: Window: Infinitely many Wieferich primes
problems.statement: The number of Wieferich primes (2^(p-1) = 1 mod p^2) below 10^4 and 10^6.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Only 1093 and 3511 are known; none other below 6.7·10^15 (Dorais and Klyve, 2011).

problems.title: Window: Wall-Sun-Sun primes
problems.statement: Every prime 5 < p < 10^6 with p^2 dividing F(p - (p/5)).
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: None is known; PrimeGrid searched to about 1.8·10^19.

problems.title: Window: Infinitely many Fibonacci primes
problems.statement: Every n < 118 with F(n) prime (certified Miller-Rabin range), and a Pratt primality certificate for F(131) = 1066340417491710595814572169.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.

problems.title: Window: Is 78,557 the smallest Sierpiński number?
problems.statement: A covering set of primes proving 78557·2^n + 1 composite for every n, and Proth primes k·2^n + 1 (n <= 500) for the odd k from 78,401 to 78,557 where she finds one.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: 78557 is Sierpiński (Selfridge, 1962); the k below it still without a known prime are 21181, 22699, 24737, 55459 and 67607 (PrimeGrid).
problems.source: Sierpiński (1960); Selfridge (1962) found the covering for 78,557.

problems.title: Window: Is 509,203 the smallest Riesel number?
problems.statement: A covering set of primes proving 509203·2^n - 1 composite for every n, and primes k·2^n - 1 (n <= 500) for the odd k from 509,001 to 509,203 where she finds one (an N+1 test beyond the Miller-Rabin range).
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: 509203 is a Riesel number (Riesel, 1956); 41 smaller k remained without a known prime in mid-2026.

problems.title: Window: Odd perfect numbers
problems.statement: The number of odd perfect numbers below 10^4 and 10^5.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: None exists below 10^1500 (Ochem and Rao, 2012).

problems.title: Window: Lehmer's totient problem
problems.statement: The number of composite n below 10^4 and 10^5 with phi(n) dividing n - 1.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Any solution is a Carmichael number with at least 14 prime factors (Cohen and Hagis, 1980).

problems.title: Window: Carmichael's totient conjecture
problems.statement: Every m < 1000 that is phi(x) for exactly one x.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Any counterexample exceeds 10^(10^10) (Ford, 1998).

problems.title: Window: Infinitely many amicable pairs

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: There are 13 amicable pairs with both members below 10^5, from (220, 284) to (79750, 88730) (OEIS A063990).

problems.title: Window: Odd weird numbers

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: None exists below 10^21 (Fang, 2022).

problems.title: Window: Brocard's problem

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: n = 4, 5 and 7; no other below 10^9 (Berndt and Galway, 2000).

problems.title: Window: Erdős-Moser equation
problems.statement: Every solution of 1^k + ... + (m - 1)^k = m^k with m <= 600 and k <= 60.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Only 1 + 2 = 3; any other solution has m > 10^(10^9) (Gallot, Moree and Zudilin, 2011).

problems.title: Window: Perfect cuboid

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The smallest Euler brick is (44, 117, 240) (Halcke, 1719); no perfect cuboid is known.

problems.title: Window: abc conjecture
problems.statement: Every coprime a + b = c with c < 6000 and quality log c / log rad(abc) at least 1.4.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: 3 + 125 = 128 has quality 1.426; the record 1.6299 belongs to 2 + 3^10·109 = 23^5 (Reyssat).
problems.source: Masser (1985) and Oesterlé (1988). Mochizuki (2012; published in Publ. RIMS, 2021) claims a proof that most experts do not accept (Scholze and Stix, 2018); Joshi (2024–2025) claims a repaired proof, also not accepted.

problems.title: Window: Beal conjecture
problems.statement: Every coprime a^x + b^y = c^z with a, b <= 120 and exponents 3 to 8.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: No coprime solution with all exponents at least 3 is known.

problems.title: Window: Fermat-Catalan conjecture
problems.statement: Every coprime a^x + b^y = c^z with a, b <= 150, exponents 2 to 9 and 1/x + 1/y + 1/z < 1.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Ten solutions are known, among them 2^5 + 7^2 = 3^4, 7^3 + 13^2 = 2^9, 2^7 + 17^3 = 71^2 and 3^5 + 11^4 = 122^2 (Beukers).

problems.title: Window: Pillai's conjecture
problems.statement: Every d <= 100 that is the difference of perfect powers u < v <= 10^10 in at least three ways, with the count.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: For d = 1 the only solution is 9 - 8 (Mihăilescu, 2002).

problems.title: Window: Sums of three cubes
problems.statement: For 1 <= n < 200 with n not 4 or 5 mod 9: which are x^3 + y^3 + z^3 with |x|, |y|, |z| <= 400, and which need larger cubes.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Every such n below 100 is now known to be a sum of three cubes (Booker, 2019; Booker and Sutherland, 2021); the open cases below 1000 are 114, 390, 627, 633, 732, 921 and 975.
problems.source: Heath-Brown (1992) conjectured it with infinitely many representations; 33 and 42 were found in 2019 (Booker; Booker and Sutherland).

problems.title: Window: Congruent number problem
problems.statement: For squarefree n <= 300: the n Tunnell's criterion excludes, the n with a rational right triangle of area n found from Pythagorean triples, and the rest.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Tunnell (1983) decides every n assuming the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.

problems.title: Window: Singmaster's conjecture
problems.statement: Every value up to 10^9 occurring at least five times in Pascal's triangle, with its multiplicity.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: 120, 210, 1540, 7140, 11628 and 24310 occur six times and 3003 eight times (OEIS A003015); no value is known to occur more than eight times.

problems.title: Window: Catalan-Dickson conjecture on aliquot sequences
problems.statement: The aliquot sequences of 276 and of 138, followed while the terms stay below 10^20.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: 138 climbs to 179,931,895,322 and ends at 1 (Lehmer); the sequence of 276 is open beyond 2000 terms.
problems.source: Catalan (1888), Dickson (1913); Guy and Selfridge conjectured the opposite.

problems.title: Window: The 196 problem
problems.statement: The reverse-and-add orbit of 196 for 3000 steps, and of 89 until it reaches a palindrome.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: 89 reaches the palindrome 8813200023188 after 24 steps; 196 has been followed for over 10^9 steps without one.

problems.title: Window: Divergent orbits of the 5x + 1 map
problems.statement: The orbit of 7 under n -> n/2 (n even), (5n + 1)/2 (n odd) for 20,000 steps: whether it repeats, and its size.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: It is believed unbounded; no 5x + 1 orbit is proved divergent (OEIS A232711).
problems.source: Folklore around the Collatz problem (see Lagarias, The 3x + 1 Problem and Its Generalizations, 1985).

problems.title: Window: Conway's amusical permutation
problems.statement: The orbit of 8 under Conway's amusical permutation (and its inverse) for 20,000 steps each way.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Conway conjectured that it never repeats (OEIS A028393).

problems.title: Window: The sixth Busy Beaver value
problems.statement: The orbit of 8 under n -> 3n/2 (n even), (3n - 1)/2 (n odd), the map behind the six-state holdout machine "Antihydra", for 20,000 steps.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: bbchallenge reports that Antihydra halts only if this orbit ever has more than twice as many odd terms as even ones; BB(6) > 2↑↑↑5 (2025).
problems.source: Radó (1962); BB(5) = 47,176,870 was proved by the bbchallenge collaboration (2024).

problems.title: Window: Covering systems with odd moduli
problems.statement: Whether one residue class for each odd divisor (> 1) of 945 can cover the integers (exhaustive), and a covering system with distinct moduli when evenness is allowed.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Erdős and Selfridge asked for an odd covering; none exists with square-free moduli (Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba, 2021), and any odd covering has lcm above 10^4 (2026 preprint).
problems.source: Erdős and Selfridge. Hough (2015) bounded the least modulus of a distinct covering system.

problems.title: Window: Infinitely many regular primes
problems.statement: The number of regular primes below 100 and 500.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The irregular primes below 100 are 37, 59 and 67 (Kummer), leaving 21 regular odd primes; Siegel's heuristic predicts a proportion e^(-1/2) = 0.6065... of regular primes.
problems.source: Kummer (1850); Jensen (1915) proved there are infinitely many irregular primes.

problems.title: Window: Kummer-Vandiver conjecture
problems.statement: Every irregular pair (p, 2k) with p <= 700: p divides the numerator of the Bernoulli number B_2k.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Vandiver's conjecture holds for every p < 2^31 (Hart, Harvey and Ong, 2017).

problems.title: Window: Infinitely many real quadratic fields of class number one
problems.statement: For squarefree d <= 3000: how many real quadratic fields Q(sqrt d) have each class number.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Gauss conjectured infinitely many real quadratic fields of class number 1.

problems.title: Window: Leopoldt's conjecture
problems.statement: Class numbers of the real quadratic fields Q(sqrt d), d <= 1500: the arithmetic of the simplest fields with infinite unit groups.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem. It views objects the problem concerns, not a finite case of it.
problems.known: Leopoldt's conjecture holds for abelian fields (Brumer, 1967), these included.

problems.title: Window: Lehmer's Mahler measure problem
problems.statement: Among reciprocal monic polynomials of degree 10 with coefficients in {-1, 0, 1}, not products of cyclotomic ones: those with Mahler measure certified below 1.18.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Lehmer's polynomial x^10 + x^9 - x^7 - x^6 - x^5 - x^4 - x^3 + x + 1 has measure 1.17628..., the smallest known above 1 (Lehmer, 1933).

problems.title: Window: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
problems.statement: For y^2 = x^3 - x and y^2 = x^3 - 25x: a_p = p + 1 - #E(F_p) for primes p <= 1500, and the product of #E(F_p)/p, Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer's original numerical evidence.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The first curve has rank 0 (1 is not congruent), the second rank 1 (5 is congruent); BSD predicts the products grow like (log p)^rank.
problems.source: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer (1960s); a Clay Millennium Prize Problem.

problems.title: Window: Littlewood conjecture
problems.statement: For x = sqrt 2 and y = sqrt 3: the n <= 10^5 minimizing a certified upper bound on n ||n x|| ||n y||, and that bound.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The exceptional set of pairs has Hausdorff dimension 0 (Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss, 2006).
problems.source: Littlewood (about 1930); Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss (2006) proved the exceptions have Hausdorff dimension 0.

problems.title: Window: Lonely runner conjecture
problems.statement: For every set of 4 distinct speeds up to 9: a rational time when every runner is at distance at least 1/5 from the start.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Proved for up to 13 runners in this convention (Sungkawichai and Trakulthongchai, 2026).
problems.source: Wills (1967); Cusick (1973). Proved for up to 13 runners in this convention (Rosenfeld, 2025; Trakulthongchai, 2025; Sungkawichai and Trakulthongchai, 2026); a September 2026 preprint claims 14.

problems.title: Window: Mahler's 3/2 problem
problems.statement: The exact set of x in [1, 100) with frac(x (3/2)^n) < 1/2 for every n < 40: its intervals, total length, and the step at which it empties (then no Z-number lies in [1, 100)).
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Mahler (1968) showed there is at most one Z-number in each interval [n, n + 1); whether any exists is open.

problems.title: Window: Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set
problems.statement: A 64 x 64 grid of parameters c around -3/4: points certified in the Mandelbrot set, certified outside, and undecided.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Local connectivity is known at many points (Yoccoz for finitely renormalizable parameters) but not in general.

problems.title: Window: Furstenberg x2 x3 conjecture
problems.statement: The minimal sets of the fractions a/10001 under x -> 2x and x -> 3x mod 1: the finite invariant sets the conjecture allows.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Rudolph (1990) proved the measure version under positive entropy.

problems.title: Window: Hilbert's sixteenth problem (second part)
problems.statement: For two Liénard systems x' = y - eps F(x), y' = -x: the hyperbolic limit cycles the averaged equation certifies for small eps.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Lins, de Melo and Pugh (1977) conjectured at most [(n - 1)/2] cycles for degree n; Dumortier, Panazzolo and Roussarie (2007) disproved it for n >= 7.

problems.known: No reference value is recorded here.

problems.known: If gamma = p/q then q > 10^242080 (Papanikolaou, 1997).

problems.known: Schanuel's conjecture would give the algebraic independence of e and pi.

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: No reference value is recorded here.

problems.known: 7,373,170,279,850 is conjectured to be the largest (Deshouillers, Hennecart and Landreau, 2000).

problems.title: Window: Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions
problems.statement: A progression of 10 primes a, a + d, ..., a + 9d.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: The primes contain arbitrarily long progressions (Green and Tao, 2008); the smallest 10-term one is 199 + 210 j.
problems.source: Erdős (1936 with Turán, and later); length 3 proved by Bloom and Sisask (2020).

problems.title: Window: Erdős-Turán conjecture on additive bases
problems.statement: For a basis of order 2 built from numbers with binary digits only in even or only in odd positions: the largest number of representations n = a + b for n <= 10^5.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: No reference value is recorded here.

problems.statement: The largest Sidon subset of {1, ..., 40}, by exhaustive search.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: A Sidon set in {1..n} of size k is a Golomb ruler of length <= n - 1; the optimal lengths for 8 and 9 marks are 34 and 44 (OEIS A003022), so the answer is 8.

problems.title: Window: Erdős-Szemerédi sum-product conjecture
problems.statement: |A + A| and |A A| for the 1000-term arithmetic progression 1..1000 and the 300-term geometric progression of powers of 2.
problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.
problems.known: Over the reals the conjecture is false (Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut and Zhelezov, 2026); for integers the best exponent is 4/3 + 10/4407 (Cushman, 2025).
problems.source: Erdős and Szemerédi (1983). Over the reals the conjecture is false (Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut and Zhelezov, arXiv 2605.28781, 2026); for integers it is open, with best exponent 4/3 + 10/4407 (Cushman, 2025).

problems.title: Window: Erdős unit distance problem: the order of growth

problems.source: Erdős (1946); disproved in May 2026 with a construction found by an OpenAI model (Alon, Bloom, Gowers, Litt, Sawin, Shankar, Tsimerman, Wang and Wood, arXiv 2605.20695; Sawin, arXiv 2605.20579).

problems.known: The optima for six and eight points are 1/8 and about 0.0724 (Comellas and Yebra, 2002).

problems.title: Window: No-three-in-line problem

problems.scope: A finite exact view: her tools compute or verify exactly what the statement says, and it settles nothing about the open problem.

needs.infinitude: A checked certificate that infinitely many integers have a property. Her checker admits finite certificates, identities on residue classes and descent on classes; none of them yields an unbounded supply of primes or solutions.
needs.prime-distribution: Explicit estimates for primes in intervals or progressions (sieve bounds with explicit constants, prime tables beyond her ranges).
needs.arithmetic-functions: Claims about sigma(n), phi(n) and other arithmetic functions for all n, beyond finite ranges.
needs.diophantine: Finiteness or nonexistence of integer solutions beyond identities on residue classes: curves of genus one and higher, exponential equations, height bounds.
needs.diophantine-approximation: Statements about how well real numbers are approximated by rationals, for all real parameters.
needs.algebraic-number-theory: Number fields, class groups, units and cyclotomic arithmetic.
needs.analytic: Complex analysis: L-functions and their zeros, contour estimates, conformal maps, zeros of polynomials.
needs.transcendence: Irrationality or transcendence certificates for specific constants.
needs.digits-normality: Statements about the digit distribution of constants.
needs.real-analysis: Inequalities, limits and extremal problems over the real numbers.
needs.harmonic-analysis: Fourier restriction, maximal functions and Kakeya-type estimates.
needs.pde: Existence, regularity and spectral properties of partial differential equations.
needs.algebraic-geometry: Varieties, cohomology theories and algebraic cycles.
needs.algebra: Rings, polynomial maps, fields and Galois groups.
needs.groups: Group presentations, finiteness questions and representations.
needs.topology: Manifolds, knots, homotopy and four-dimensional topology.
needs.geometry: Points, distances, packings, coverings and convex bodies in Euclidean space.
needs.graphs: Graphs with colorings, minors, labelings, cycles and Hamiltonian paths.
needs.set-systems: Families of sets, hypergraphs, partial orders and matroids.
needs.additive-combinatorics: Sums, products and arithmetic progressions in sets of integers, for all sets.
needs.finite-search-at-scale: A finite question whose resolution needs a search far beyond her work bounds, with a checkable certificate such as a SAT proof log or an exhaustive-search receipt. Her SAT tool checks RUP proof logs, but only small ones.
needs.big-integers: Primality proofs and arithmetic for integers far beyond her bounds.
needs.unbounded-orbits: A certificate that an orbit never terminates or grows without bound; her descent language certifies only that orbits fall.
needs.dynamics: Continuous, holomorphic or measure-theoretic dynamical systems.
needs.complexity: Computational complexity classes and lower bounds.
needs.operator-theory: Operators on infinite-dimensional Hilbert and Banach spaces.
needs.designs: Combinatorial designs: Hadamard matrices, projective planes, orthogonal Latin squares.
needs.mathematical-physics: Rigorous quantum field theory and fluid equations.
needs.covering-systems: Finite systems of congruences covering the integers. Her language has residue classes but no claim kind for a covering system.
needs.statement-bounds: Stateable with her claim kinds but beyond the bounds of her problem statements. Widened: numerators up to 64 and least n up to 100,000 (they were 16 and 1000).

census_q.summary: Tallies and member lists of integers satisfying a predicate in her typed expression language.

primes_q.summary: Prime tallies, record gaps, Goldbach tables and Gilbreath rows.

arith_q.summary: Divisor-function tallies, totient fibres and odd weird numbers.

dioph_q.summary: Solutions of Diophantine equations in boxes: power sums, abc triples, Euler bricks, three cubes, congruent numbers.

bigint_q.summary: Lucas-Lehmer, Pepin, Wall-Sun-Sun and Proth and N+1 tests, and Pratt certificates.

orbit_q.summary: Bounded runs of orbits: reverse-and-add, residue-class maps, aliquot sequences, Conway's permutation.

covering_q.summary: Covering systems and covering sets of primes, found or excluded exhaustively.

field_q.summary: Class numbers, irregular pairs and small Mahler measures.

zeta_q.summary: Interval arithmetic for zeta and L-functions: signs on the critical line, zero counts, sizes, lattice point errors.

const_q.summary: Rigorous enclosures of constants: continued fractions, excluded rationals, relations and polynomials.

interval_q.summary: Exact sets of reals as rational intervals (Mahler's Z-numbers).

approx_q.summary: Littlewood products and lonely runner times.

dynamics_q.summary: Certified Mandelbrot points, x2 x3 orbits and averaged Liénard zeros.

spectrum_q.summary: Eigenvalue counts of discrete Laplacians by exact inertia.

lattice_q.summary: Lattice partition functions and Galerkin conservation identities.

knot_q.summary: Jones polynomials, the Kashaev invariant of the figure-eight knot and inscribed squares.

graph_q.summary: Graph invariants, witnesses and exhaustive census over small graphs.

setsys_q.summary: Census over small set systems and partial orders, and sunflower-free families.

additive_q.summary: Prime progressions, Sidon sets, sums and products, four cubes.

design_q.summary: Hadamard matrices, projective planes and orthogonal Latin squares.

sat_q.summary: SAT witnesses and RUP-checked refutations of finite encodings.

circuit_q.summary: Exact circuit sizes, graph isomorphism and small unique games.

algebra_q.summary: Galois groups, polynomial inverses, matrix multiplication schemes and Casas-Alvero searches.

variety_q.summary: Point counts over finite fields and rational points.

config_q.summary: Geometric configurations checked exactly: unit distances, packings, kissing, Borsuk parts, sphere energies.

statement_bounds.summary: Wider bounds for unit fraction statements: numerators up to 64, least n up to 100,000.

esq.summary: Certified exception sets of a/n as a sum of three unit fractions up to 2a^2 + 1: a complete divisor-method search for each exception and an exact witness for every other n.

resolved.title: Moving sofa problem
resolved.statement: The largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around a right-angled corner in a hallway of unit width is that of Gerver's sofa, about 2.2195.
resolved.resolution: Proved by Jineon Baek (arXiv 2411.19826, 2024); two independent Lean formalizations were completed in 2026. Uniqueness of the optimal sofa is open.

resolved.title: Cycle double cover conjecture
resolved.statement: Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles covering each edge exactly twice.
resolved.resolution: A proof generated by an OpenAI model was released in July 2026 with a Lean formalization, and independent expositions by Geelen and by Oum (arXiv 2607.15399, 2607.16356); not yet refereed.

resolved.title: Chvátal's conjecture
resolved.statement: In every down-closed family of sets, some largest intersecting subfamily consists of the sets containing one common element.
resolved.resolution: Proved by Fan Chang, Hong Liu and Miao Liu (arXiv 2609.19123, 2026), with a short spectral proof by Ellis, Filmus and Friedgut (arXiv 2609.28404); both formalized in Lean, neither refereed yet.

resolved.title: Sendov's conjecture
resolved.statement: If all zeros of a complex polynomial of degree at least 2 lie in the closed unit disc, each zero is within distance 1 of a zero of its derivative.
resolved.resolution: Proved for all degrees by Lech Mazur (August 2026, computer-assisted, found with AI help), formalized in Lean; Tao (2020) had proved it for sufficiently large degree.

resolved.title: Schiffer's conjecture
resolved.statement: If a Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded planar domain is constant on the boundary, the domain is a disc.
resolved.resolution: Disproved in 2026: a Lean-formalized non-disc counterexample by Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont, and independently a computer-assisted one by Colbrook and Stepaniants (arXiv 2608.01579), which also disproves the planar Pompeiu conjecture.

resolved.title: Irrationality of zeta(5)
resolved.resolution: A preprint by A. Fauzan (September 2026) with a complete Lean formalization whose check against the formal-conjectures statement passes; the paper is unrefereed.
resolved.source: Apéry proved zeta(3) irrational (1978); Zudilin (2001) showed one of zeta(5), zeta(7), zeta(9), zeta(11) is irrational.
